outcome.answer:
Content creators can use recommendation-system transparency and observability methods to see what factors drive exposure and why items get little visibility. One paper proposes a surrogate model that explains item exposure at a system level by approximating the exposure distribution and identifying the most influential features behind recommendation decisions [1]. Another presents a counterfactual observability framework for creators that estimates what the recommender would have done in the absence of a content item or model decision, helping attribute outcomes beyond raw views and clicks [2].

If the issue is that an item was ranked below another, a pairwise counterfactual method can explain why item A was ranked higher than item B by identifying profile items that contributed to the relative ranking [4].
